item.title: [LU-19932] client write hang in osc_extent_wait()
item.description:
I was testing out a workload that was reported in GitHub:

# python
Python 3.9.17 (main, Aug  9 2023, 00:00:00) 
[GCC 11.4.1 20230605 (Red Hat 11.4.1-2)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import numpy as np
>>> data = np.random.random((6000, 500, 40))
>>> np.save("/mnt/test.npy", data)

on a recent build (2.17.50-85-gc606081, Ubuntu 6.8.0-88-generic x86_64 kernel).

This is trying to do a single 3GiB write() system call. In the GitHub issue, strace is showing a fault returned to the caller:

write(4, "\360\313"..., 3072000000) = -1 EFAULT (Bad address)

In my testing (possibly affected by kernel or Lustre version), rather than returning an error my python3 process hung in IO (unkillable idle sleep) after having written out about 1GiB of memory:

# pgrep python

GDB shows this to be at wait_event_idle() in osc_extent_wait():

# gdb lustre/osc/osc.ko
(gdb)  list *(osc_extent_wait+0x44f)
0x3019f is in osc_extent_wait (/usr/src/lustre-head/lustre/osc/osc_cache.c:994).
989		if (rc == 0) {
990			OSC_EXTENT_DUMP(D_ERROR, ext,
991				"%s: wait ext to %u timedout, recovery in progress?\n",
992				cli_name(osc_cli(obj)), state);
993	
994			wait_event_idle(ext->oe_waitq,
995					smp_load_acquire(&ext->oe_state) == state);
996		}
997		if (ext->oe_rc < 0)
998			rc = ext->oe_rc;

and indeed this error message was printed on the client console:

LustreError: 627533:0:(osc_cache.c:990:osc_extent_wait()) extent 000000000fdab39e@{[228352 -> 229375/229375],
    [3|1|-|active|wiuY|00000000d732b228], [4218880|1024|+|-|00000000ab2def22|1024|0000000000000000]}
    myth-OST0002-osc-ffff89deea9bf000: wait ext to 0 timedout, recovery in progress?
LustreError: 627533:0:(osc_cache.c:990:osc_extent_wait()) ### extent: 000000000fdab39e ns: myth-OST0002-osc-ffff89deea9bf000
    lock: 00000000ab2def22/0xd01e87e953e26bd2 lrc: 4/0,1 mode: PW/PW res: [0x2c0000400:0x3d757:0x0].0x0
    rrc: 2 type: EXT [0->18446744073709551615] (req 0->4095) gid 0 flags: 0x800020000020000 nid: local
    remote: 0x198a66a0ec5e0d26 expref: -99 pid: 627533 timeout: 0 lvb_type: 1 lru_score: 4 lru_type: 1

It isn't clear why the process is waiting, since the client and server are both responsive to all other commands (ls -l on the file, etc).

status.description: This issue was once resolved, but the resolution was deemed incorrect. From here issues are either marked assigned or resolved.

comments.comment: This code was changed from using l_wait_event() with LWI_INTR() (interruptible sleep) to wait_event_idle() in patch https://review.whamcloud.com/35971 ("LU-10467 lustre: use wait_event_idle() where appropriate"). It is worthwhile to change this back to an interruptible sleep, but that doesn't address the core issue of why the IO never completes.

"Andreas Dilger <adilger@thelustrecollective.com>" uploaded a new patch: https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/64250
Subject: LU-19932 osc: restore interruptible waits on client
Project: fs/lustre-release
Branch: master
Current Patch Set: 1
Commit: 7a635020fb4adfeabe71cd8d3ab52acb143b68dc

It looks from the console messages and if I read OSC_EXTENT_DUMP() correctly, that oe_state=1 ("active") and it is waiting for state=0. The system is still running if there is interest to debug something live, but I'm not sure what to check next.

jinshanx I was looking at your old patch https://review.whamcloud.com/8656 ("LU-4198 clio: generalize cl_sync_io") while trying to restore the ability to interrupt a stuck IO.

Your old patch is removing the call to `cl_io_cancel()` (which was the only caller of this function, and was eventually removed in later patches), and it appears that the code now just waits forever until the IO is finished (which may never happen) and can never be interrupted, rather than trying to abort the in-flight IO and then exit quickly with an error. There were some later changes to the waiting functions, but I think 8565 is the patch that fundamentally broke being able to interrupt an IO in cl_sync_io_wait().

Changing the (existing) `wait_event_idle()` to `l_wait_event_abortable()` allows the wait to be interrupted, but it immediately crashes in several sanityn test cases like:
https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sets/f50e770b-a2d5-4bc6-8dd7-40240778c241

LustreError: 265444:0:(cl_io.c:1239:cl_sync_io_wait()) ASSERTION( atomic_read(&anchor->csi_sync_nr) == 0 ) failed: 
CPU: 0 PID: 265444 Comm: rw_seq_cst_vs_d Kdump: loaded Tainted: G           OE     -------- -  - 4.18.0-553.89.1.el8_10.x86_64 #1
Call Trace:
dump_stack+0x41/0x60
lbug_with_loc.cold.7+0x5/0x43 [libcfs]
cl_sync_io_wait+0x384/0x3c0 [obdclass]

generic_file_buffered_read+0x5eb/0xbb0
vvp_io_read_start+0x6a2/0x880 [lustre]
cl_io_start+0x61/0x130 [obdclass]
cl_io_loop+0x9e/0x220 [obdclass]
ll_file_io_generic+0xb7d/0x11f0 [lustre]
do_file_read_iter+0x951/0xfe0 [lustre]
new_sync_read+0x10f/0x160
vfs_read+0x91/0x150

I looked at restoring the cl_io_cancel() call to cl_sync_io_wait() but its function arguments no longer exist after your patch 8656. I'm wondering if there is some other function that could be called to actively cancel the in-flight pages? Something like the following to clean up all the pages? or will that have other fallout?

        anchor->csi_sync_rc = rc;
        anchor->csi_end_io(env, anchor);

Alternately, find the right arguments to call cl_io_cancel() again...

OCI has a Customer hitting this issue with Lustre 2.16.59 clients as well.
One more observation we had for 2.17 clients, disabling hybrid I/O avoids the issue. Running the repro given in the ticket after disabling hybrid I/O didn't encounter the issue.
lctl set_param llite.*.hybrid_io=0
Very odd to be running 2.16.59 - that's a development version, not a release version!

Yeah agreed, The customer chose that version on their own.
We are now suggesting them to use 2.17 with the workaround of just disabling hybrid I/O for now.

This issue does appear to be a duplicate of LU-19536; Andreas I don't want to lose the restore interruptible wait patch, but I feel this should be closed as a dupe in service of clarity...?

I'm going to do that and we'll figure out that patch.
See LU-19536.
